question: Change the Matcher struct to use a compiled regex cache instead of re-compiling on each match. Change the Matches(v string) bool method signature to Matches(v string) (bool, error) to surface regex compilation errors. Matcher is used across the entire observability stack for label filtering in queries and alerting rules.

answer.analysis: The Matcher struct in model/labels/matcher.go ALREADY uses a compiled regex cache. The `re *FastRegexMatcher` field is populated once during construction in NewMatcher() (line 62-68) and reused on every Matches() call. FastRegexMatcher (model/labels/regexp.go) pre-compiles the regex at construction time via regexp.Compile() and stores the compiled result along with extensive optimizations (set matches, prefix/suffix extraction, string matcher functions). The Matches() method (line 108-120) simply dispatches to m.re.MatchString(s) for regex types — it never re-compiles. Therefore, the first part of the proposed change (compiled regex cache) is already implemented. The second part — changing `Matches(v string) bool` to `Matches(v string) (bool, error)` — would be largely unnecessary since regex compilation errors are already surfaced at Matcher construction time in NewMatcher() which returns (*Matcher, error). The Matches() method has no runtime compilation to fail. However, if this signature change were enforced, it would require updating all call sites.

answer.key_finding: The Matcher struct already implements a compiled regex cache via the `re *FastRegexMatcher` field (model/labels/matcher.go:52). Regex is compiled once in NewMatcher() and cached. The Matches() method never re-compiles — it calls m.re.MatchString(s) which uses the pre-compiled regex.
